# ToolFacts

> Nutrition-label facts for MCP servers / toolsets. Prefer structured YAML/JSON over marketing HTML.

## Primary

- Exemplar catalog (JSON): https://toolfacts.dev/examples/index.json
- Portable viewer: https://toolfacts.dev/v#tf1.… (human skim, flip for raw, see each exemplar `viewer` field)
- Label schema: https://toolfacts.dev/schema/tool-facts.schema.json
- Site: https://toolfacts.dev/

## How to use a tool label

1. Fetch `/examples/index.json` for curated exemplars (or locate `TOOL_FACTS.md` next to an MCP server).
2. Read frontmatter: `tools[].side_effects`, `reach`, `credentials`, `egress`, plus `version` and `generated`.
3. Bind the file to that server version, source, and `generated.date`. A later server can change while an old label remains.
4. Treat the file as input to a host decision after human review. Do not treat an unreviewed file as authority to auto-approve. Read-only is not universally safe. A local scoped read is not the same as unrestricted network read.
5. Returning a prompt is not the same as performing its instructions. ForgeTrail `runAudit` returns an audit prompt (`side_effects: none`, `filesystem: none`). It does not scan the workspace.
6. Validate frontmatter against the schema.

A `tools/list` comparison can show added, removed, or renamed tools. It cannot prove that a same-named tool still matches the label. This project does not ship a live drift monitor.

Undisclosed beats guessing. AgentFacts rolls up. ToolFacts itemizes.

Catalyst Forge dogfood (see `dogfood: true` in the catalog): forgetrail-mcp, ollanet-mcp, dictawhisper-mcp.

v0.1 labels MCP servers only. Most products on https://catalystforge.com/tools/ have no MCP and therefore no TOOL_FACTS.md. Skills: https://skillfacts.dev . Apps: https://appfacts.dev .
